text: . US President Donald Trump said that the United States has reached a deal with Denmark to strengthen the American military presence in Greenland, ending months of tension over his repeated calls to acquire the Arctic island.The agreement leaves Greenland under Denmark’s sovereignty while giving the US what Trump described as a larger security role. In a social media post, Trump said the agreement gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland, completely addressing all of US concerns.Denmark said the agreement will be signed by the governments of the US, Denmark and Greenland next week during the United Nations General Assembly, although it will still need parliamentary approval in Denmark and Greenland before it can take effect. Danish and Greenlandic leaders said the deal protects sovereignty and self-determination, while the US presented it as a major national security gain.Since returning to the White House last year, Trump has pressed Denmark to sell Greenland to the US, arguing that the island is vital to American security. He had also refused to rule out taking it by military force, even though Denmark is a NATO ally. Denmark and Greenland repeatedly said the island was not for sale and criticised reports that the US was gathering intelligence there. Russia and much of Europe also strongly opposed the US push.

. Devotees thronged temples across North India today to mark the auspicious occasion of Radha Ashtami with religious fervour and devotion. A massive influx of devotees also gathered at the Shri Radha Rani Temple in Uttar Pradesh’s Barsana, Mathura, Vrindavan and other parts of the Braj region.According to Hindu mythology Radha Rani was born in Barsana. Radha Ashtami is traditionally observed as the arrival day of Radha Rani. Devotees observe a fast on the occasion and worship Radha and Lord Krishna according to religious rituals, with the belief that such devotion brings love, happiness and peace into their lives.

. Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya congratulated Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa K Vinod on winning a silver medal in the Women’s 10m Air Rifle Team event at the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, Dr Mandaviya wished the champions and the entire Indian contingent many more moments of glory.

. The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has revised hallmarking charges for gold and silver articles. The hallmarking fee for gold has been increased from 45 to 75 rupees per article, while the charge for silver remains unchanged at 35 rupees per article. The revised charges will come into effect immediately, ahead of the festive season.The increase in gold hallmarking charges has been notified through the BIS (Hallmarking) Amendment Regulations, 2026, dated 14th of this month.Under the amended Schedule IV, jewellers will have to pay a hallmarking fee of 75 rupees per gold article, subject to a minimum charge of 200 rupees per consignment. For silver articles, the fee payable by jewellers to recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centres (AHCs) remains 35 rupees per article, with a minimum charge of 150 rupees per consignment.BIS hallmarking verifies the purity of precious metals used in jewellery and certifies the article under the Bureau of Indian Standards. A hallmarked article carries three key markings: the BIS logo, the Karat fineness, and a six-digit alphanumeric Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number.

. The Indian Navy’s guided-missile frigate INS Trishul made a port call at Alexandria, Egypt from 14th to 17th of this month as part of her deployment. In a statement, the Defence Ministry said that the ship was accorded a warm welcome with the Egyptian Naval Ship Al Qadeer escorting it on arrival at Alexandria Harbour. The Commanding Officer and crew of INS Trishul paid homage to the Bravehearts of the two World Wars at the Chatby War Memorial. The War Memorial contains 12 burials and bears the names of 19 Indian soldiers who died in ships sunk in the Eastern Mediterranean.The Ambassador of India to Egypt, Suresh Reddy, visited INS Trishul and interacted with the ship’s crew. During the interaction, he highlighted the importance of the Indian Navy’s presence in the region.INS Trishul undertook a Passage Exercise with Egyptian Navy Ship ENS Bernees. The exercise involved coordinated manoeuvring drills, communication exercises and approaches for replenishment at sea. It provided an opportunity for personnel of both navies to exchange professional expertise and enhance interoperability.

. India’s textile exports increased to over 29,700 crore rupees in August this year as compared to over 25,600 crore rupees during same month of the last year. The Ministry of Textiles said that the exports increased by 16.1 per cent as compared to August 2025. It added that during April-August 2026, cumulative textile exports reached over 1,40,000 crore rupees, registering growth of 10.3 per cent over the corresponding period of the previous year.The Ministry said that the sustained growth across major segments reflects the increasing competitiveness and diversification of India’s textile export basket. It added that the growth is supported by improved market access, policy interventions and continued efforts towards value addition and market diversification.

. The Indian tennis team was knocked out of the 2026 Davis Cup after suffering a 3-1 defeat to the Republic of Korea in their second-round qualifier in Seoul today. Sumit Nagal’s singles loss handed the hosts an unassailable lead and secured their place in the Final 8.India, who began the day trailing 2-0 after losing both opening singles matches yesterday, briefly revived their hopes when N. Sriram Balaji and Dhakshineswar Suresh won the doubles match to reduce the deficit. However, world No. 157 Kwon Soon-woo defeated India’s top-ranked singles player Nagal 6-1, 6-2 to seal the tie for South Korea, who will compete in the Final 8 in Bologna, Italy, in November.The defeat means India will have to compete in the first round of the 2027 Davis Cup Qualifiers. World No. 49 doubles pair Balaji and Suresh had kept India in contention with a 6-3, 3-6, 6-3 victory over South Korea’s Nam Ji-sung and Park Ui-sung.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Keralam, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands today. The Met Department has predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Madhya Maharashtra, Odisha, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal till tomorrow. The IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into the Andaman Sea till tomorrow and the East Central and adjoining Northeast Bay of Bengal for the next two days.

. Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah today said that disaster early warning systems will be implemented as a top priority following devastating floods in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli river basins that caused extensive loss of life and infrastructure damage.Addressing the nation on Constitution Day, Balendra Shah said Nepal must adopt a proactive approach to disaster management, with greater focus on risk reduction, preparedness and response. He said the country’s vulnerability to disasters requires stronger preparedness before disasters strike.A flash flood hit riverside settlements in Rasuwa district on the 26th last month, rapidly affecting neighbouring areas including Nuwakot and Dhading. According to the latest figures from Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, 13,756 people have been rescued, while 6,055 remain out of contact. A total of 1,410 bodies have been recovered, with several victims identified and their remains handed over to their families.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah today paid tribute to Pandit Shriram Sharma Acharya on his birth anniversary. In a social media post, Mr Shah said that through the establishment of the All World Gayatri Pariwar, Pandit Shriram Sharma Acharya paved the way for the cultural upliftment of society. He noted that by harmonizing science and spirituality, Pandit Acharya brought the wisdom of eternal culture to every individual. The Home Minister highlighted that with the mantra ‘Hum Badlenge, Yug Badlega’ he inspired millions of people toward public service and social reform. Mr Shah added that his life and values will forever remain a guiding light for the nation and society.

. India has been ranked first in business climate among forty plus global markets in the latest Business Climate Survey 2026 by the Swedish Chamber of Commerce in India. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal shared this information in a social media post. He said India’s business climate is setting the gold standard for stability, growth and ease of doing business amid global turbulence.The Global Business Climate Survey 2026 edition presents insights from 41 markets, offering a broad view of Swedish companies’ perspectives on doing business abroad. The survey aims to provide a framework for comparing economic performance, outlook, and operating conditions over time in key Swedish export markets. It highlights the challenges companies face and identifies opportunities for Swedish companies considering entry into new markets or expansion in existing ones.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow. The Met Department has predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Madhya Maharashtra, Odisha, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and  Karaikal for the next two days.The Weather Department also advised Fishermen not to venture into the Andaman Sea from today till next Monday and the East central and adjoining northeast Bay of Bengal for next three days.For Delhi, IMD has forecast a partly cloudy sky tomorrow. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 33 to 35 degrees Celsius while the minimum temperature will hover around 23 to 25 degrees Celsius tomorrow.

. The Government has announced the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Awards for the year 2024. The awards recognise outstanding achievements by individuals in the field of adventure and seek to promote a spirit of endurance, risk-taking, teamwork and quick and effective decision-making in challenging situations. The awards are given in four categories, which are Land Adventure, Water Adventure, Air Adventure and Lifetime Achievement. Each awardee will receive a statuette, a certificate and award money of 15 lakh rupees. The awardees are Baljeet Kaur and Skalzang Rigzin in Land Adventure category, Rimo Saha in Water Adventure category and Shiv Prasad Chamoli in the Life Time Achievement category.The selections were made following the recommendations of the National Selection Committee. The Committee evaluated the nominations and recommended the awardees for conferment of the national honour.The awards seek to promote among the youth a spirit of courage, endurance, discipline, risk-taking and cooperative teamwork, while encouraging the ability to respond with speed and effectiveness in challenging situations. President Droupadi Murmu will confer the awards along with the National Sports Awards 2025. The date of the award ceremony will be announced later.

. The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

. US President Donald Trump has said that he is forming an AI Force and will announce an AI Czar in the near future. In a post on his Truth Social account, Trump said he would not stand by and let the decimation or destruction of AI happen. Mr Trump has also described AI as the next Industrial Revolution and said that it could possibly account for as much as 25 per cent of US gross domestic product. In his post, Trump claimed that the destruction of AI was one of the many hoaxes that the Democrats have been propagating. Along with it, he named the Russia-Ukraine war and global warming as hoaxes that have been “destroying” the United States.Trump did not provide details on the structure of the planned AI Force or the role of the AI Czar. The announcement comes amid growing debate in the United States over the rapid development of AI and its potential risks. Earlier this week, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said that the United States cannot afford to lose the artificial intelligence race to China, while promising action against Chinese individuals and companies that steal from American technology businesses.

. In the Chess Olympiad, the Indian men’s team defeated Spain 3-1, with world champion D Gukesh leading the way with a clean victory over former world championship challenger Alexei Shirov in Samarkand yesterday. Meanwhile, R Praggnanandhaa was held to a draw by David Anton Guijarro, while Nihal Sarin also settled for a draw against Jaime Santos Latasa. In the women’s section, India recorded a 3-1 victory over Mongolia. B Savitha Shri continued her impressive run with her fourth consecutive win, defeating seasoned player Munguntuul Batkhuyag.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices today ended almost flat. The Sensex dipped 22 points to close at 74,315. The Nifty added 53 points to settle at 23,271.In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index gained 0.9 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index added 0.8 per cent.Earlier, the markets opened mildly lower after a hawkish stance from the US Federal Reserve and concerns over geopolitical developments. However, both the indices soon recovered and traded with gains for most of the volatile session, supported by value buying.In the Sensex pack, 21 out of 30 companies logged gains. Among the top performers, Tata Steel climbed 2.8 per cent, Bharat Electronics Limited surged 2.4 per cent and Indigo gained 2.3 per cent. In contrast, HDFC Bank declined 1.3 per cent, Titan dipped over 1.1 per cent and ICICI Bank fell one per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 18 out of 28 sectors edged upward. Among the top gainers, Insurance advanced 3.2 per cent, Capital Goods jumped nearly two per cent, and Industrials gained one and a half per cent.  In contrast, Top 10 Banks declined 0.7 per cent, Private Banks Index shed 0.6 per cent and Bankex dropped half a per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was positive, as shares of 2 thousand 686 companies advanced, 1 thousand 642 declined and 207 remained unchanged.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has cautioned that the semiconductor industry should be prepared for cyberattacks and any kind of disruption by countries that do not want India to move up the semiconductor value chain.Talking to a media house in New Delhi, Mr Vaishnaw said India has to continuously be watchful of the potential geopolitical risks that will arise because it is now emerging as a country that can design and manufacture chips. He added that this will be seen as a threat by many other established players. Mr Vaishnaw said it is an industry which requires lots of effort on every front. He added that the industry, the government, and the state governments have to work in tandem.

. Iran has communicated its conditions to international mediators for restarting negotiations with the United States. It has also warned that Tehran is prepared for a decisive war if Washington rejects its demands. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said Iran’s conditions included an end to the war on all fronts, the release of frozen Iranian funds and an end to the naval blockade.In a separate post on X, Rezaei said Iran has announced seven conditions for beginning negotiations with Washington and described Tehran’s position as clear and unambiguous. The Iranian security chief said Tehran’s planning is focused on US naval assets stretching from the Gulf through the Gulf of Oman and into the Arabian Sea. He claimed Iran had also recently test-fired a multi-warhead anti-ship missile near a US vessel or aircraft carrier.Rezaei warned that any future Iranian response could be extensive, targeting US bases in the region as well as American commercial interests and companies operating locally. International Mediators have been working to re-establish negotiations between the two sides since their memorandum of understanding expired last month. Regional countries are also seeking an end to the war that began when the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in late February, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

. President Droupadi Murmu will address the valedictory session of the International Conference on The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics this evening in New Delhi. The two-day Conference is being organised by the National Green Tribunal (NGT). During the session, Union Minister of Power Manohar Lal, Supreme Court Judge Justice B.V. Nagarathna, Chairperson of NGT Justice Prakash Shrivastava and Solicitor General of India, Tushar Mehta, are likely to be present.The Conference on the Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics provided a platform for the exchange of judicial approaches, scientific knowledge, environmental governance practices and institutional experiences across jurisdictions. The conference witnessed the participation of environmental experts, Judges of the Supreme Court of India and High Courts, District Court Judges, Secretaries of various Ministries, senior government officials and other stakeholders.It also brought together eminent Judges and judicial representatives from 17 countries. It facilitated dialogue on critical environmental and climate challenges, including gaps in policy formulation, implementation and enforcement, and explore ways to strengthen environmental governance and institutional cooperation.

. India will host the Asian Senior Wushu Championships for the first time in 2028, with around 500 athletes from 42 countries across Asia expected to participate in the prestigious continental competition.The decision was officially approved at the Wushu Federation of Asia (WFA) Congress held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. In another significant development, Bhupender Singh Bajwa of the Wushu Association of India was nominated as a member of the Executive Committee of the Wushu Federation of Asia during the Congress. The 11th edition of the championship is expected to bring together not only athletes but also coaches, judges, technical officials and sports administrators from across the continent.

. India secured the silver medal in the women’s 10m air rifle team event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, with Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod combining to deliver the country’s first medal of the Games. The Indian trio finished with a team total of 1898 points, placing them behind China in the standings.The Indian teqball player Quimcy Dsouza missed out on a women’s singles bronze medal after suffering a 2-0 defeat to home favourite Yuina Sakamoto in a closely contested match. Sakomoto prevailed 12-11, 12-11 in a match that saw both games go down to the wire, leaving Dsouza to rue several missed opportunities. The Indian had chances to take control of the contest, holding set point in the opening game before Sakamoto fought back.Dsouza also established a lead in the second game and even saved a match point with a winning serve, but was unable to close out the contest as Sakamoto capitalised on crucial errors at the decisive moments. However, Dsouza will have another opportunity to claim a medal, as she is set to compete in the mixed doubles bronze medal match alongside Mohamed Anas Beg.In hockey, the India women’s team began their Asian Games 2026 campaign with a dominant 19-0 win over Uzbekistan in their Pool B opener at Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium in Japan today. Deepika Sehrawat was the star of the match as she scored eight goals. Ishika Chaudhary scored three, while Lalthantluangi and Neha each bagged two.India will next take on Indonesia tomorrow. The opening result gave India an early platform in the tournament, with their forwards and penalty-corner attack both making an immediate impact. The match marked Savita Punia’s 320th senior international cap. She joined Vandana Katariya as the joint-most capped Indian women’s hockey player. Meanwhile, Baljeet completed her 50th senior international cap.

. The Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat- 100 Weeks Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan will witness a major nationwide youth mobilisation today. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh is being organised across 1,067 locations in the country.It added that this programme will be organised across 471 District MY Bharat Offices, along with 596 locations of partner organisations. The Samaroh will bring the campaign’s message directly to young people through Nasha Mukt Pledge, Signature Campaign, thematic street plays, slogan writing and youth-led discussions.

. Indian embassies in Bahrain, Kuwait and UAE organised several community-focused activities as part of Seva Pakhwada –  highlighting themes such as fitness, environmental awareness, cleanliness, civic participation and community engagement.In Bahrain, the Embassy of India organised the Viksit Bharat Run, bringing together around 200 members of the Indian diaspora, including members of Samskruthi Bahrain. The three-kilometre run was followed by a collective recitation of the Viksit Bharat pledge and a ‘Swachhata Hi Seva’ campaign where community members participated in a park cleaning drive.In Kuwait, the Embassy, in association with ARMS4U and KIPCO Group, organised a tree plantation drive under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign. The initiative brought together community members and partners with the shared objective of honouring mothers through a meaningful act of planting trees. More than 30 Indian community associations participated, planting over 60 saplings to promote greener public spaces and environmental sustainability.In UAE,the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi marked Seva Parv, commemorating Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 25 years in public service with members of the Indian Community.Several school students participated in the programme, along with various organisations including Indian People’s Forum (IPF), Indian Business & Professional Council (IBPC), Indian Business and Professional Group (IBPG) and ICAI.The Indian community joined in these programmes with great enthusiasm and in the spirit of unity. More suchprogrammesare planned in other places in West Asia in the coming days.

. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju today attended the opening Ceremony of the Korfball Premier League 2026 at Thyagaraj Indoor Stadium, New Delhi. In a social media post, Mr Rijiju said that it was wonderful to witness the growing enthusiasm for Korfball in India. He said that sports like these open new avenues for the youth, promote fitness and teamwork as well as strengthen India’s growing sporting ecosystem.

. The United States has urged its citizens to reconsider travel to and through West Asia amid heightened regional tensions, warning of possible rapid escalation, flight disruptions and attacks targeting US interests, as Yemen’s Houthi fighters launched missile and drone attacks towards Saudi Arabia.In a worldwide caution issued by the US State Department, Americans in West Asia were advised to exercise heightened vigilance and remain prepared for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures and other travel disruptions. The department also warned that Iran and groups supportive of Tehran could target US interests, businesses and institutions overseas. For Saudi Arabia, the US State Department has maintained a Level 3 – Reconsider Travel advisory. The department cites the risk of Iranian drone and missile attacks targeting American interests, armed conflict, terrorism, exit bans and local laws concerning social media activity.The warning came as Saudi Arabia reported that a ballistic missile launched by Yemen’s Houthis towards Riyadh was intercepted. The Saudi-led coalition also said the Houthis attempted to target civilian infrastructure in Bisha, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed grief over the sudden demise of journalist Payal Mehta today. In a social media post, the Prime Minister described her as a hard-working journalist who remained firmly connected to the ground, bringing a deep understanding of national issues to her reporting.He added that beyond her work, she will be remembered for the kindness and warmth with which she touched so many lives. Expressing condolences to her family, friends and colleagues, Mr Modi wished god to grant them strength in this difficult hour. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw today expressed grief over the demise of journalist Payal Mehta. In a social media post, Mr Vaishnaw said that her dedication to reporting was exemplary.Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has expressed grief over the demise of journalist Payal Mehta today. In a social media post, Mr Singh said that Payal Mehta was an extremely hard-working and dedicated journalist who covered the Parliament beat with great commitment and professionalism. The Minister added that during Parliament sessions, she would be present from early morning till late at night, tirelessly following the proceedings and doing her work with remarkable dedication. He extended condolences to her family and friends in this difficult hour and wished the god to provide them strength to bear this irreparable loss.Senior journalist Payal Mehta passed away in Mumbai early this morning. She was 46. Ms Mehta, who was visiting the city, rushed to a hospital after experiencing sudden uneasiness early in the morning, where she later breathed her last.

. In Men’s Cricket, India crushed Afghanistan by 127 runs in the third T20I to complete a 3-nil series sweep in New Delhi last night. Put in to bat, India posted 221 runs for the loss of seven wickets in stipulated 20 overs. In reply, Afghanistan were bowled out for 94 in 14.1 overs. Earlier, Afghanistan won the toss and opted to bowl.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has extended his best wishes to the Indian contingent as the Asian Games commenced today in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. In his message, Mr Modi said each athlete has worked incredibly hard and shown remarkable dedication and determination and India is proud of them. He hoped that the athletes play well and shine at the Games.
. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold was one per cent up at 1,52,362 rupees per 10 grams. Silver rose 1.1 per cent to 2,31,337 rupees per kilogram.

. The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is set to become the third member of his family to address the United Nations General Assembly when he is expected to deliver his maiden speech at the 81st session in New York on September 24.Tarique’s father Shaheed President Ziaur Rahman addressed the General Assembly during its 11th Special Session in 1980. In his address, Ziaur Rahman had focused on the widening gap between rich and poor countries, poverty and hunger, economic development and the need for greater international cooperation.Thirteen years later, Ziaur’s wife Khaleda Zia addressed the General Assembly during its 48th session in 1993. She subsequently addressed General Assembly proceedings on several other occasions, including the commemorative meeting marking the 50th anniversary of the United Nations in 1995, the 27th Special Session on Children in 2002, and two separate meetings during the 60th session in 2005.Now, Tarique Rahman is preparing to take the same international platform for the first time as Prime Minister of Bangladesh.According to State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam, the Prime Minister is scheduled to leave Dhaka for New York on September 21 to attend the 81st session of the UN General Assembly and is expected to address the Assembly on September 24.State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said the Prime Minister would present Bangladesh’s new outlook and future vision before the world leaders, highlighting the country’s democratic transformation, future development priorities, global peace and sustainable solutions to international crises.He said poverty eradication, economic prospects, climate action and climate finance would also feature in the address, while the Rohingya crisis would remain a major priority during the visit.The 81st session carries additional significance for Bangladesh as Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman is serving as President of the General Assembly.

. Vultures are extremely important for our ecosystem. By feeding on dead animals, they help keep the environment clean and reduce the spread of harmful diseases.However, vulture populations have declined significantly because of habitat loss, poisoning, and certain veterinary medicines that are harmful to them. Conservation efforts are therefore essential to protect these birds and maintain the balance of nature.On this International Vulture Day, government and environmental experts have urged people to understand, protect, and conserve vultures for a healthier environment.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. Thirty-six sportspersons and three coaches from Manipur are representing India at 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya in Japan. The Games kicked off today and will continue till 4th October. The Games bring together athletes from across Asia in one of the continent’s largest multi-sport events.The sportspersons from Manipur are part of India’s 499-member contingent participating in Sepaktakraw, Rowing, Cycling, Fencing, Canoeing & Kayaking, Boxing, Weightlifting, Wushu, Judo and Hockey. The 36 athletes comprise 12 in Sepaktakraw, 1 in Rowing, 3 in Cycling, 3 in Fencing, 6 in Canoeing & Kayaking, 1 in Boxing, 3 in Weightlifting, 3 in Wushu, 1 in Judo and 3 in Hockey.Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh congratulated all the sportspersons and coaches on earning the opportunity to represent the country at the Asian Games. He encouraged them to compete with confidence, discipline and determination and to give their best in their respective events.

. SEMICON India 2026, the fifth edition of India’s flagship semiconductor conference, concluded successfully at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi yesterday. The three-day conference under the theme “Silicon to Systems: Building the Ecosystem” featured over 600 exhibitors. These included around 300 international participants, representatives from 52 countries, and over 150 speakers. Six Country Pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, along with 12 State Pavilions, showcased different dimensions of the semiconductor value chain.The event recorded 51,656 total registrations and cumulative footfall of about 40,000. Prime Minister Narendra Modi had inaugurated SEMICON India and highlighted India’s progression from policy discussions and project planning to commercial semiconductor production. He interacted with young chip designers and students and virtually inaugurated commercial production lines at CDIL Semiconductor, Mohali, and Suchi Semicon, Surat. The three days witnessed 56 MoUs, announcements and strategic initiatives, spanning semiconductor design, fabrication, advanced packaging, equipment and materials, power electronics, and Artificial Intelligence.

. In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. The Archaeological Survey of India has notified Gollala Gudi Temple at Palampet in the Mulugu district of Telangana as a monument of national importance. The Ministry of culture said that the temple is situated near the UNESCO listed Ramappa Temple and is renowned for its exquisite carvings and architectural heritage.The temple is a Trikutalaya and consists of a mandapa facing East and surrounded by three garbhagriha.A monument of national importance in the country is protected under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958. The Archaeological Survey of India takes charge of such sites for conservation, maintenance, and regulated public access

. Today is World Suicide Prevention Day. The day is observed worldwide to raise awareness about suicide prevention and the importance of mental health.The occasion reminds us that people facing emotional distress or difficult circumstances need timely support, understanding and appropriate care. Experts emphasise that listening to someone with patience and without judgement can encourage them to seek help and support.On this Day, people are encouraged to remain attentive to the emotional well-being of those around them and, when required, guide them towards family members, trusted persons or mental health professionals.

. India and Nepal discussed measures to facilitate greater market access for products of both countries. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry in a statement said that during the two day meeting of Inter-Governmental Sub-Committee (IGSC) on Trade, Transit and Cooperation to Control Unauthorised Trade which concluded yesterday both sides reviewed a wide range of issues. It was related to market access, Customs and trade facilitation, standards, food safety, border infrastructure, rail and road connectivity and other trade-related matters.The Indian delegation was led by Joint Secretary in the Department of Commerce, Ujjwal Kumar Ghosh, while the Nepali delegation was led by Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Buddha Bahadur Gurung. The meeting focused on facilitating legitimate trade while strengthening mechanisms to ensure compliance with applicable rules and prevent misuse of preferential trade arrangements. Both sides also reviewed rail and road connectivity, movement of freight, Integrated Check Posts and land-port infrastructure.The discussions focused on improving the utilisation of existing infrastructure and addressing operational bottlenecks affecting bilateral and transit trade. The Ministry said that India and Nepal share close historical, cultural and economic ties and the discussions at the IGSC are expected to further strengthen bilateral trade, transit connectivity and economic cooperation between the two countries.

. The global ratings agency Moody’s today raised India’s real GDP growth forecast to 7 per cent, ​from its earlier projection of 6 per cent for the current financial year. The agency said that the upward revision reflects the resilience of the Indian economy amid the global shock caused by the conflict in West Asia.The agency expects India to continue growing faster than all other G20 economies. Moody’s said India’s real GDP growth rose to 8.2 per cent year-on-year in the first half of 2026, compared with 7.3 per cent in 2025. The growth was supported by stronger private consumption, robust investment, continued government spending on infrastructure, a revival in private investment and sustained strength in the services sector. However, Moody’s has warned of risks to the outlook.El Niño-related disruptions could push up food prices and affect private consumption. Higher energy and fertiliser import costs, weaker external demand and lower remittances from West Asia could also widen the current account deficit and slow economic growth.

. India has dispatched another 11 tonnes of relief material to Nepal, including medicines, forensic supplies, tents, hygiene kits, sleeping bags and other essential supplies. This was the 9th Indian Air Force plane carrying relief material to support Nepal’s recovery. In a social media post, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar said that India continues to support Nepal’s recovery.Nepal faced devastating floods last month, disrupting life and property.

The Enforcement Directorate (ED), Delhi Zonal Office, has provisionally attached equity shares of a company having a current market value of more than Rs 42 Crore, in connection with an alleged large-scale financial fraud involving a collective investment scheme.ED initiated the investigation based on an FIR registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation. Subsequently, CBI filed a charge-sheet and a supplementary charge-sheet against 33 accused persons for their role in running the illegal investment scheme.According to the charge-sheets, the accused entities and persons were fraudulently mobilising over Rs 48,000 crore from lakhs of investors across India under the pretext of sale and development of agricultural land. Investors were induced to invest and made to sign misleading documents, such as agreements, powers of attorney, and other instruments. In most cases, land was never delivered, and approximately Rs 48,000 crore remains unpaid to investors.ED has attached over 29.46 lakh equity shares of the company, purchased for more than Rs 30 Crore. The agency alleged that the funds used for the purchases were diverted from money mobilised from gullible investors. Further investigation is in progress.

. The government has said that Biometric Aadhaar authentication is mandatory for subsidised domestic LPG refills from 1st October this year. Domestic LPG consumers will need to have completed Biometric Aadhaar Authentication to book refills at the regulated Retail Selling Price with applicable subsidy.Biometric Aadhaar Authentication ensures that subsidised LPG reaches only genuine and deserving households. Linking each connection to the Aadhaar-authenticated consumer will help prevent diversion of subsidised domestic cylinders for commercial and industrial use. It will remove duplicate and ineligible connections, and make subsidy delivery transparent and targeted. The Ministry said the process is not meant to deny LPG to any genuine household, and every eligible consumer has several easy ways to complete it.It said 27.43 crore consumers have already completed authentication and do not need to do anything further. Authentication can be completed at the time of delivery, at the distributor’s showroom, or on Oil Marketing Company (OMC) mobile apps. The Petroleum and Natural Gas Ministry has urged consumers who have not yet completed Biometric Aadhaar Authentication to do that before 1 October 2026.

Nepal government has formed a seven-member expert panel to investigate the causes behind last month’s devastating floods, which killed more than 1,400 people and left over 6,000 missing.According to an official, the Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation has formed the panel comprising experts in hydrology, glaciology, remote sensing, geology, hydropower infrastructure and disaster risk reduction. The panel will seek to determine what exactly led to the devastating flash flood in the Bhotekoshi river on August 26, how the disaster unfolded and whether climate change played a role. It will also examine the possible links between glacial, geological and hydrological hazards. The panel has been asked to submit a preliminary report within a month.

. The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek has concluded with 13 key outcomes. The outcomes cover counter-terrorism, climate action, energy, disaster management and digital cooperation.The summit adopted the historic Bishkek Declaration, marking the SCO’s 25th anniversary. It also approved four MoUs and more than 20 decisions.A major decision was to include English as an official SCO language. Leaders also agreed to establish a Universal Centre for Countering Security Threats.The measures will strengthen cooperation against terrorism, extremism, organised crime and other transnational threats. They will also improve security information sharing.Several decisions focus on tackling drug trafficking and synthetic drugs. These include stronger coordination among law enforcement agencies and a cooperation programme on combating drug addiction until 2030. The measures support India’s efforts against cross-border narcotics trafficking and narco-terrorism.On climate and energy, SCO members agreed to enhance cooperation on energy conservation and efficiency. They also adopted a memorandum on combating climate change. These measures support India’s energy security and climate-resilient development goals.The summit also adopted a statement on assistance to countries affected by emergencies. It will strengthen cooperation in disaster management and humanitarian assistance, an area where India has significant capabilities.In the digital sector, members agreed to expand cooperation in artificial intelligence. The move will provide India an opportunity to share its digital and AI expertise and promote responsible and inclusive use of the technology.An agreement on information cooperation will also promote institutional exchanges and help strengthen India’s engagement with the regional media space.The Ministry of External Affairs said the outcomes give India a strategic platform to advance its positions on regional security, development and connectivity. They also strengthen India’s engagement with Central Asia and the wider Eurasian region.The MEA said, addressing the summit, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called for a roadmap for the next 25 years. He stressed the need for concrete outcomes in the areas of security, connectivity and opportunity.The two-day SCO Summit was held at Bishkek in Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1.

. Global crude oil prices declined today. Brent crude was trading 1.2 per cent down at 107 US dollars and 44 cents per barrel in intra-day trade at a time of writing this report. Meanwhile, West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 1.8 per cent lower at 103 US dollars and 93 cents per barrel.

. The 20th Asian Games officially got underway today at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium in Japan, with Emperor Naruhito declaring the Games open. The two-hour ceremony was attended by Japan’s royal family, Games officials, and  Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) President Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani.India’s 501-member contingent was led by double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat during the athletes’ parade. Sehrawat replaced shot putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor as flag-bearer after the latter did not receive his ceremonial kit on time.Some events have already begun, including women’s cricket, where India have already advanced to the semifinals after an eight-wicket win over Japan yesterday. India will face Bangladesh in the second semifinal in Nisshin, Japan, tomorrow. In Teqball, which is making its Asian Games debut, India’s Quimcy D’Souza suffered a 1-2 defeat to Indonesia’s Ima Sumaya in the women’s singles semifinal and will play Japan’s Yuina Sakamoto for bronze medal tomorrow.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has extended his best wishes to the Indian contingent as the Asian Games commenced today in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. In his message, Mr Modi said each athlete has worked incredibly hard and shown remarkable dedication and determination and India is proud of them. He hoped that the athletes play well and shine at the Games.

. Saudi Arabia has confirmed that Yemen’s Houthi rebels tried to attack its capital with a ballistic missile. The statement by the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis came long after the morning attempt, which the coalition said was intercepted. It was the first attack targeting Riyadh since the escalation in fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and Yemeni government forces backed by the Saudis.The statement also said the Houthis tried to attack civilian infrastructure in the Red Sea port city of Yanbu and in Taif, Baysh and Farasan, but they were thwarted, giving no further details. The Houthis earlier claimed, without providing evidence, that they had targeted sensitive sites in Riyadh and facilities of Saudi oil giant Aramco in Yanbu, causing massive fires.
